newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Diebold CEO sees ATM growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Diebold CEO sees ATM growth.

text.p: Diebold Inc chief executive officer Robert Mahoney said he sees continued healthy demand for the company's main products, automated teller machines and similar items, despite more than 20 years of proliferation.
He also said the Canton, Ohio-based company's 1996 net sales will be about $1 billion versus $863.4 million in 1995.

"This year we'll be around $1 billion in revenue," Mahoney said in an interview. He declined to comment on First Call's earnings estimates of $2.05-$2.08 a share for 1996, but said: "The analysts who follow Diebold are very good."
Mahoney, also chairman and president, said Diebold has met or exceeded earnings estimates for the last five or six years.
Asked if ATMs were nearing a saturation point, he said markets are strong in both developed and emerging nations.
Banks are replacing earlier models and installations in supermarkets, airports and malls provide "really high growth" in the U.S. and other developed countries.
"It's pretty hard to look out beyond five years, but I see nothing but continued growth in...ATM markets."
ATMs, cash dispensers and servicing of those products account for about 70 percent of revenues, he said.

Last year, the financial industry accounted for more than 90 percent of consolidated revenues, operating profit and identifiable assets, the annual report said. It also said Diebold is developing ATM-type machines to sell concert tickets, securities and other items.
Mahoney said about 65 percent of overall revenues come from products and 35 percent from technical service.
Diebold, which launched international sales in 1881 by selling a safe to Mexico's president, has joint ventures in China, India and Venezuela and is exploring Brazil, he said.
